Cat Detective Privacy Policy

Updated: November 23, 2026

No separate game registration is required. The app tries Google sign-in at startup, but cancellation, failure or offline use still allow local play; cloud saving is a separate choice. New installations default to contextual ads. You can play and use investigation points without watching rewarded ads.

Version note: 1.0.0 build 10 introduces automatic Google sign-in and a contextual-ad default, without a startup ad-choice prompt or a new Choose later option. Build 9's three choices and previously saved deferrals are distinguished below. Android backup exclusions apply from build 9. This notice does not mean a public release is complete.

1. Scope and operator

TeamCP develops and operates Cat Detective for Android (com.teamcp.catdetective). This policy explains the game's data processing and your choices. Contact: teamcp.channel@gmail.com.

There is no separate game account or developer-operated game server. The app does not ask you to enter your name, email or telephone number, and does not collect Google passwords or payment card/bank details. If you email support, your reply address and message are used to handle your inquiry.

2. Information on your device

Android app-private storage supports play, resuming progress and preventing duplicate rewards. Ad choices stay on each device; there is no separate consent-record server. The release app does not send answer-tap coordinates or response-time analytics to an external server and does not use Firebase Analytics.

Version 1.0.0 configures app files and preferences to be excluded from Android automatic backup and device transfer. This is not a guarantee about every manufacturer's transfer behavior. Use optional Google saving to transfer progress.

  • The current run, completed stages, records, case/collection/daily/tutorial progress
  • Investigation point earnings, spending and claimed ad rewards
  • Language and sound settings, app sign-in and Google save connection state, explicit ad choice, disclosure version and last-choice time

3. Automatic Google sign-in and optional saving

From build 10, normal startup checks existing Google Play Games authentication and requests the Google sign-in screen once if needed. Google processes authentication and account identifiers during this process. Cancelling sign-in or an authentication/communication failure leads to local play; you can reconnect in Settings.

Successful authentication checks whether a cloud save exists, but sign-in alone does not upload local progress or overwrite an existing save on first connection. Loading, transferring device progress and deleting the cloud save are separate choices. A previously enabled save connection attempts automatic sync. Conflicting point-spending records require a choice.

Saved data includes cumulative stage completion, records, daily/collection/practice progress, point spending and reward claims. The current run, app settings, ad choice, photos, audio and screenshots are not in this snapshot.

Logging out in Settings disconnects the app's saving connection and leaves you at the title. It does not delete the device's Google Account or existing progress. Tapping Start or launching the app again retries Google sign-in. Google authentication and ad personalization are separate.

4. Ads and information processed

The 1.0.0 ad configuration uses Unity LevelPlay and Unity Ads, without AdMob, Google UMP or the AdQuality SDK. See Unity's policy below for providers involved in ad delivery, mediation and measurement.

On a new build 10 installation, the contextual default may start the ad SDK and preload ads before you make a choice. A previously saved Choose later state is an exception and is preserved. Rewarded hints, continues and bonuses are optional. Banners may appear in the lobby, settings, cases, daily, collection, practice introduction and results, but not the title, title sign-in or actual play, including loading, answers and continues.

  • IP address and IP-based approximate location; device model, OS/app version, language and network information
  • Device, advertising and SDK user identifiers, where device settings and applicable law permit
  • Ad requests, impressions, clicks, completions, errors and diagnostics
  • The purchase-history category in Unity Ads disclosures; Cat Detective itself has no real-money purchases

Purposes include ad delivery, frequency management, measurement, fraud prevention and diagnostics. Scope varies by region, device, choices and service. Google and ad services may perform their own diagnostics and product improvement; TeamCP does not operate a game-behavior analytics server.

5. Your advertising choices

Build 10 applies contextual ads without a startup prompt. This automatic default is not recorded as affirmative consent or as a user-choice timestamp. Settings offers two ad modes. Personalization choices from older disclosures become contextual; only an explicit choice under the current disclosure is retained as personalized.

A Choose later state already saved in build 9 or another earlier build is preserved after updating. In that state, the ad SDK is not initialized and ads are not requested or displayed. Explicitly choosing either ad mode in Settings enables ads; build 10 has no button to defer again.

Changing modes prevents the app from reusing previously prepared ads and late reward callbacks. Switching to contextual ads does not shut down an SDK already running, cancel every transmission or erase data already sent.

The contextual default still involves data processing and does not replace any legally required consent or checks for minors. Android advertising ID/privacy settings, provider rights procedures below and our contact address remain available.

  • Contextual ads (default): denies personalization consent and sends sale/sharing opt-out signals. It does not stop all data processing, including possible access to advertising identifiers.
  • Personalized ads allowed: sends personalization consent only when you explicitly choose it under the current disclosure. You can withdraw personalization consent by switching to contextual ads in Settings.

6. External services and overseas processing

Google Play Games and Unity services have their own policies. Their roles and processing vary by account, ad and service; not every provider acts solely as TeamCP's processor.

Cloud and advertising information may be processed outside your country. Provider policies linked below explain recipients, processing locations, transfer safeguards and processing grounds. This notice does not replace any consent required for particular processing or transfers.

TeamCP does not keep copies of progress/ad identifiers on its own game server or sell a separate customer list. Advertising processing may nevertheless count as a legal ‘sale’ or ‘sharing’ where applicable. See the ad restriction signals and providers' opt-out and rights instructions.

Detailed notice of overseas transfers (added November 23, 2026)

Under Articles 28-8 and 30 of Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), we list each kind of processing in this game in which personal information is transferred outside Korea. The information below is sent directly from your device to each provider without passing through any server operated by TeamCP. Provider details are based on each provider’s published policy.

Ads — Unity LevelPlay, Unity Ads, ironSource Ads

Recipient and contact
Unity Technologies (Unity Technologies S.F.) — operator of Unity LevelPlay, Unity Ads and ironSource Ads
Contact: DPO@unity3d.com · 116 New Montgomery Street, Suite 200, San Francisco, CA 94105, United States
Destination countries
The United States, plus countries where Unity has facilities (including Israel, where ironSource is headquartered) and countries with data centers of service providers Unity uses (such as Google Cloud Platform) — as stated in Unity’s Game Player and App User Privacy Policy
Data transferred
Advertising identifiers (Google advertising ID, app set ID, etc., to the extent device settings allow), IP address and approximate location derived from it, device model, operating system, app version, language, network information, and ad request, impression, click, completed-view, error and diagnostic information (details in the ads section of this policy)
When and how
Each time the ad SDK initializes or requests, shows or measures an ad while the app is running, sent directly from your device to Unity’s servers over the internet (encrypted connection)
Purpose
Ad mediation and delivery, frequency capping, performance measurement, fraud prevention, error diagnosis
Retention period
Unity states that it keeps data for as long as needed for the processing purposes and may keep it longer when needed for legal obligations or for disputes or investigations (Unity policy section 10, “Retention”). Because Unity does not publish a fixed retention period for general ad data, this policy does not state a separate period.
Legal basis
PIPA Article 28-8(1)(iii)(a) — treated as outsourcing and storage needed to perform the contract for providing a free (ad-supported) game, with the transfer details disclosed in this policy
How to refuse and effect
If you turn off the internet connection, no ad requests or transfers take place. If you delete the advertising ID in Android settings, the advertising ID is not sent. If you do not want any transfer, you can stop using and uninstall the app; in that case you cannot use ads or ad rewards. To access or delete information already transferred, contact Unity (DPO@unity3d.com) or use the privacy icon in the ad.

Google — Google Play Games

Recipient and contact
Google LLC
Contact: googlekrsupport@google.com · Domestic representative in Korea: Google Korea LLC (22F, 152 Teheran-ro, Gangnam-gu, Seoul · +82-2-722-7778 · data-access-requests@google.com) — as stated in Google’s “Additional privacy information for Korean residents”
Destination countries
Google data centers outside Korea (such as the United States). See Google data center locations for where they are.
Data transferred
Google Play Games: (Google Play version only) Play Games sign-in status and player identifier, and, if you choose Google saving, cumulative progress snapshots (completed stages, records, daily, collection and practice progress, point use and reward records)
When and how
Sent to Google over the network (encrypted connection) at the same time the information is collected, when the feature is used (per Google)
Purpose
Google sign-in and optional cloud save and load
Retention period
Google account and Play Games data are kept until you delete them or for the period Google sets (“Retaining your information” in Google’s Privacy Policy).
Legal basis
PIPA Article 28-8(1)(iii)(a) — treated as outsourcing and storage needed to provide the game-linked features you choose, with the transfer details disclosed in this policy
How to refuse and effect
If you cancel sign-in or sign out in settings, you can play with on-device progress without Play Games transfers. In that case you cannot save and load across devices. Saved data can be deleted with the cloud-save delete option in the app settings or by deleting your Google Play Games data.

The following processing takes place in Korea and is not an overseas transfer.

  • ONE store in-app payments (ONE store version): payments are processed by ONE store Co., Ltd. (Republic of Korea), and this game does not transfer payment information abroad.

7. Deletion and retention

Local progress/settings remain until you delete them; there is no automatic 90-day deletion. Changing an ad choice updates the current choice and last-choice time. Provider policies govern cloud/ad retention periods, criteria and legal/security exceptions.

  • Device data: uninstall the app or clear its data in Android settings. This may be irreversible, so first check whether any progress you want to keep has been saved.
  • Google cloud progress: connect in Settings, select Delete cloud save and confirm. This deletes Cat Detective's snapshot and disconnects automatic sync, not your local progress/current run or Google Account. Reconnecting and transferring later can create a new save.
  • Without the app: use the Google Play Games deletion instructions below to manage this game's data. This is different from deleting your entire Google Account.
  • Advertising data: use the ad's privacy icon or the access/deletion instructions in Unity's policy below. Uninstalling, logging out or limiting ads does not itself erase data already processed by a provider.
  • Deletion help: email teamcp.channel@gmail.com with the game name and data type (device/Google/ads). Do not send passwords, verification codes or unnecessary identity documents. For data TeamCP does not hold, we direct you to the provider's verification/deletion process.

8. Choices and rights

Depending on applicable law and processing conditions, you may have rights of access, correction, deletion, restriction, objection, portability, consent withdrawal, sale/sharing opt-out or complaint to a supervisory authority. Not every right applies identically to all processing.

Contact us with the game name, request type and reply address. Do not send sensitive documents first. Providers may need their own identity checks for data they hold. Google connection and ad-personalization consent are not required to play, but default contextual ads on a new installation may still process information.

9. Young players and guardians

Cat Detective is intended for teenagers aged 13 and older and adults, not specifically for children. An all-ages content rating does not establish eligibility to consent to data processing. Rules for minors, guardian consent and advertising vary by region.

The app does not collect dates of birth/identity documents or verify guardian consent. This policy and the ad-choice buttons are not substitutes for that verification. Contact us for questions or deletion assistance.

10. Security and changes

Local information is stored in Android app-private storage. Google saving and advertising transmissions use the respective providers' security mechanisms.

When features, SDKs or processing change, we update this policy and its date and announce important changes in the app or here. Each language page covers the same scope; you can contact us about translation differences.

Additional notice under Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act (added November 23, 2026)

Under Article 30 of Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) and Article 31 of its Enforcement Decree, this notice explains your rights and how to exercise them, children under 14 and their legal guardians, the security measures we take, and our privacy officer. It applies together with the rest of this policy.

Your rights and how to exercise them

  • You may at any time ask TeamCP to give you access to, correct, delete, or suspend the processing of the personal information it processes about you, and you may withdraw your consent (PIPA Articles 35–37).
  • How to ask: email the app name and your request to the contact below (teamcp.channel@gmail.com). Because the app has no accounts, please include information that lets TeamCP find the record (for example, the approximate date or report number of a problem report). A legal guardian or a person you authorize may also make a request; in that case we may ask for proof of that relationship.
  • Response time: we will tell you the outcome within 10 days of receiving your request. If the law gives a reason to limit or refuse the request, or we cannot complete it within that time, we will tell you why and how to object.
  • Information stored only on your device (app records, settings, and so on) is not held by TeamCP, so you can delete it yourself with the app’s delete options, by clearing the app’s storage in Android settings, or by uninstalling the app.
  • For information processed by outside providers such as the ad services and Google, you can also contact each provider at the contact listed in the overseas transfer notice above.
  • Remedies in Korea: you can apply for dispute mediation or advice to the Personal Information Dispute Mediation Committee (+82-1833-6972, www.kopico.go.kr), the Personal Information Infringement Report Center (118, privacy.kisa.or.kr), the Supreme Prosecutors’ Office (1301, www.spo.go.kr), or the Korean National Police Agency (182, ecrm.police.go.kr).

Children under 14 and legal guardians

  • Korea’s Personal Information Protection Act requires the consent of a legal guardian when the personal information of a child under 14 is processed on the basis of consent (Article 22-2).
  • This app does not ask for a date of birth or age, and it has no age check or way to confirm a guardian’s consent. Because it does not treat users differently by age, the processing described in this policy also applies to users under 14. The app tells the ad services, at app level, that it is “not directed to children”. This is not the result of checking any individual user’s age.
  • Personalized ads: on a new install, non-personalized ads are the default, and personalized ads apply only if you choose them yourself in settings. Users under 14 should keep the default.
  • Users under 14 should not include personal information such as their name or contact details in problem reports or inquiries.
  • Guardians’ rights and how to exercise them: a legal guardian may ask for access to, correction, deletion, or suspension of processing of the child’s personal information, and may withdraw consent. The method and response time are the same as in “Your rights and how to exercise them” above. We ask only for the minimum information needed to confirm guardianship and delete it once confirmed.
  • If we learn that the personal information of a child under 14 has been processed without a legal guardian’s consent, we will promptly delete that information held by TeamCP.

Security measures for personal information

  • On-device storage: app records and settings are stored in the app-private storage that Android keeps separate for each app, and are not sent to servers operated by TeamCP except as described in this policy.
  • Encrypted transmission: information the app sends over the internet (ad requests, Google services) is sent over encrypted connections (HTTPS/TLS).
  • Data minimization: we do not collect sign-ups, passwords, names, or phone numbers, which keeps the personal information held by TeamCP to a minimum.
  • Retention and deletion: TeamCP does not run a server that receives game records; information on your device stays there until you delete it.
  • Inquiry emails are deleted once they are no longer needed after we have responded. Personal information is kept only as electronic files and is deleted when the retention period ends.
  • Security for information processed by outside providers such as the ad services and Google follows each provider’s policy.
